summary: Mary Clabaugh Wright was a sinologist and historian. She studied at Vassar College and Radcliffe College before serving as curator of Stanford's China collection (1947) and later as associate professor (1959) and full professor (1964) at Yale University.

Specializing in religious studies, sinology, and japanology, Mary Evelyn Tucker studied at SUNY, Sophia University, Fordham, and Columbia (PhD). She served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell University (1989–2005) and became a professor at Yale University around 2006.

Mary Haas was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, where she studied under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935). She later held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1941–1977).
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Ross Bolleter and, attested in 2007, studied under Peter Harvey at the University of Sunderland.

Mary Shepherd Slusser worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan, Columbia University (PhD), NYU, and Harvard. Her career included posts at the U.S. Department of State (1951–1958) and National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).
Marybeth White works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned an honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University in 2006.

Maryla Falk worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1933–1939) and was later a member of the Polish Oriental Society and a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She was mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as assistant and assistant professor at Kyoto University (1968; 1981–1993) and as professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Gadjin Nagao, and others. He taught in Kyoto University's Faculty of Letters (1961–1988).

Masaaki Nitta is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).
Masaaki Noni is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He served as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
Masaaki Sugiyama was a historian of Iranian, Central Asian, and Chinese history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1981 to 1992.
Masaaki Tsuchiya is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979–1989) and was appointed to a post at Senshu University around 1996.

Masaharu Anesaki worked in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo and under scholars including Deussen and Rhys Davids in Europe, he became a professor (1904) and library director (1923–1934) at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. After studying at Tokyo University of Education, he held an assistant professorship at Ibaraki University (1977) and later became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba (2006).

Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Koyasan University and Kanazawa University, becoming a professor there around 2008.
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies at Ryukoku University and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1981 to 1991.

Masahiro Inami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University (~1985–1990) and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei University attested around 1996 and 2009.

Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1947–1953), where he later served as chief professor of religious studies and religious history from circa 1972 to 1985.
